metadata.title: Derivative as Slope: The Tangent Tells the Story
metadata.subject: Mathematics
metadata.objective: Show a tangent line whose slope matches the derivative at a movable point.
metadata.learner: Can read coordinates on a graph.
misconceptions: Derivative is the value of the function
A positive derivative means the function is positive
expectedUnderstanding: The tangent line at a point has slope f'(p), so its steepness is the derivative there.
The sign of the slope says whether the function is rising or falling, not whether f is positive or negative.
Where the tangent is flat the derivative is zero even when f itself is large.

properties.label: Point position p on the curve

primitives.text: The derivative is the tangent's slope, not the function's value
flat tangent here, and f is at its largest
grey legs: run of 90 px, rise set by the slope
Move p: on the rising part f' is positive; past the crest f' is negative while f is still positive

controls.label: Slide the point along the curve

checkpoints.title: One point, one tangent
checkpoints.body: The blue point sits on f(x) = 1.6 sin x. The violet line just touches the curve there: it is the tangent, and its steepness is the derivative.

checkpoints.title: Rise over run
checkpoints.body: The grey legs form a small right triangle under the tangent. Its rise over its run is exactly the slope f'(p), so a steep tangent means a large derivative.

checkpoints.title: Sign is about direction, not height
checkpoints.body: The black needle shows the sign of the slope. Just past the crest the curve is still positive, yet the needle points down because f is falling. Derivative is not the function's value, and a positive derivative does not mean f is positive.

checkpoints.title: Find the flat spot
checkpoints.body: Slide p to about 1.57, the crest. The tangent goes horizontal and the needle collapses to zero, even though f is at its maximum. Slope zero and value zero are different things.

narration.text: One point on the curve, and one line that just grazes it: the tangent.
The rise over that little run is the tangent's slope, and that slope is the derivative at the point.
Watch the sign needle. Past the crest the curve is still above the axis, but the slope is negative, so the needle points down.
At the very top the tangent is flat. The derivative is zero there even though the function is at its biggest.

fallback.text: Static figure. A sine-like curve f(x) = 1.6 sin x drawn across the frame with a horizontal axis. A blue point sits at position p on the curve, with a violet tangent line through it. A small right triangle under the tangent shows a horizontal run and the corresponding rise. On the right, a vertical needle shows the sign of the slope: up when f is rising, down when f is falling, zero at the crest. The slope at p is 1.6 cos p.

accessibility.alt: A curve f(x)=1.6 sin x with a movable point p. The tangent line there has slope 1.6 cos p, also shown as a rise-over-run triangle. A vertical needle shows the slope sign by direction, not color: up while the curve rises, down while it falls, and it shrinks to nothing at the crest.
